question: Can a neural-network pruning criterion retain cross-parameter curvature without materializing the full Hessian by decomposing supported feed-forward graphs into series and matrix-multiplication interactions and propagating Jacobian-vector products?

key_findings.claim: OBA assigns each weight a local first-plus-second-order score while avoiding explicit construction of the full Hessian.
key_findings.evidence: For perturbation delta-theta, the method targets the coordinatewise product delta-theta_i times (H delta-theta)_i in addition to the first-order Taylor term. Theorems 4.2 and 4.4 split cross-layer terms into series paths and pairs of branches feeding a matrix multiplication. Jacobian-Vector Product Forward Propagation then propagates the summed directional input perturbation through the graph, and Algorithm 1 realizes the resulting score with forward and backward passes. The experiments set delta-theta_i equal to theta_i, corresponding to deleting the parameter in the paper's sign convention.

key_findings.claim: The advertised exactness is narrow: OBA targets an exact Hessian-vector contribution at the evaluation point, not the exact loss change caused by a finite pruning operation.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 3 is a Taylor expansion with an omitted higher-order remainder, and Equation 4 explicitly discards that remainder. Moreover, Equation 3 gives the quadratic loss contribution as one half delta-theta-transpose H delta-theta, whereas the coordinate expression in Equation 4 has no one-half factor. A constant factor would not change a pure quadratic ranking, but it changes the relative weighting when the first-order term is retained. Scores are also averaged from finite training batches before many parameters are pruned together.

key_findings.claim: The proof does not establish an exact Hessian-vector product for every parameter as broadly stated because it drops mixed derivatives involving an upper-layer bias on an invalid independence argument.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix E.1 states that the mixed derivative with respect to a lower-layer weight and an upper-layer bias is zero because those parameters are independent. Parameter independence does not imply that a shared loss has zero mixed derivative; even a two-layer scalar linear network with squared loss generally has a nonzero lower-weight/upper-bias mixed Hessian entry. The resulting formulas and Algorithm 1 propagate upper-layer weight perturbations while setting the corresponding surrogate bias to zero. This does not negate the weight-only empirical criterion, but it narrows the theorem's claim over theta, which was defined to contain weights and biases.

anchors.section: Appendix E.1, opening paragraph and Lemma E.1

key_findings.claim: On the selected ResNet32 neurons, OBA gives the strongest per-layer Spearman correlation with measured loss-change ranks and is less sensitive than several baselines to the chosen cross-layer normalization, although it is not best in every all-layer cell.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports per-layer correlations of 0.443 on CIFAR-100 and 0.421 on CIFAR-10 for OBA, higher than Weight, Taylor, OBS, OBD, and EigenDamage in those rows. Across all-layer normalizers, OBA ranges from 0.444 to 0.500 on CIFAR-100 and 0.379 to 0.456 on CIFAR-10. OBD reaches 0.541 under CIFAR-100 l2 normalization and Taylor reaches 0.444 under CIFAR-10 standardization, so the evidence supports robustness rather than universal cellwise dominance.

key_findings.claim: In the reported ImageNet structured-pruning runs, OBA preserves more top-1 accuracy than the listed criteria at approximately matched FLOP speed-up on both ResNet50 and ViT-B/16.
key_findings.evidence: At 2.00 times speed-up, OBA's ResNet50 accuracy is 75.62%, 0.53 points below the 76.15% dense value; the closest listed result is C-OBS at 75.48% and 2.01 times. On ViT-B/16, OBA reaches 79.64% at 1.30 times speed-up, 1.43 points below dense, compared with Taylor at 77.65% and 1.31 times and Weight at 77.03% and 1.32 times. These are accuracy/FLOP comparisons, not measured end-to-end latency comparisons.

key_findings.claim: The CIFAR one-shot tables favor OBA in several severe-pruning settings, but one highlighted numerical claim in the prose is not recoverable from the displayed table.
key_findings.evidence: Table 3 reports that the severely pruned CIFAR-10 ResNet32 produced by OBA retains 93.45% accuracy with 94.51% FLOP reduction, versus a displayed dense baseline of 95.30%, a 1.85-point drop. The preceding prose instead says the small approximately 6%-remaining-FLOP setting loses only 0.79%. No displayed OBA/baseline pair in that ResNet32 block yields 0.79 points, so that sentence should not be used as a quantitative finding without clarification from the authors.

key_findings.claim: OBA is substantially stronger than the reproduced baselines at high unstructured sparsity in the reported ResNet20 and ResNet50 experiments, but its advantage is relative to each method's own dense checkpoint.
key_findings.evidence: At 90% sparsity on CIFAR-10 ResNet20, OBA retains 86.27% accuracy, or 94.80% of its 91.00% dense accuracy, while CHITA++ retains 79.32%, or 86.82% of its 91.36% dense accuracy; Weight retains 67.00%. On ImageNet ResNet50 at 80% sparsity, OBA retains 47.14%, or 61.92% of its 76.13% dense accuracy, while CHITA-BSO++ retains 26.21%, or 34.03% of its 77.01% dense accuracy. The paper explicitly switches to within-method accuracy ratios because dense starting accuracies differ.

key_findings.claim: OBA's importance acquisition is materially more expensive than ordinary training and several pruning criteria, with attention's parallel term accounting for almost half of the reported ViT cost.
key_findings.evidence: Table 6a reports 4.027 seconds per ViT-B/16 pruning iteration: 0.799 seconds for upper-series terms, 1.166 for lower-series terms, and 1.944 for parallel terms, compared with 0.252 seconds for regular training. ResNet32 totals 2.072 seconds versus 0.326 seconds for regular training. For the CIFAR-100 structured workflow, the authors estimate about 4.2 hours from 200 batches and 50 pruning iterations; their plot places OBA above Taylor, OBD, OBS, and EigenDamage in score-acquisition time.

method.core_idea: Use local curvature to rank deletions without forming the full Hessian: compute each supported parameter's directional Hessian contribution by propagating perturbations through the graph, then aggregate those scores over structurally coupled pruning groups.
method.mechanism: The paper sets a deletion-direction perturbation proportional to each current parameter. It records layer-output loss gradients, backpropagates surrogate upper-layer weight perturbations for upper-series terms, and uses a forward-mode Jacobian-vector recurrence to accumulate how all lower-series parameter perturbations change each layer input. For two branches joined by matrix multiplication, it adds cross-branch parallel terms; the ViT implementation specializes this calculation to attention's Q, K, and V paths. Per-weight contributions are summed over each DepGraph-coupled output/input channel group, normalized within a group, globally ranked, and pruned either once or iteratively with fine-tuning. Unstructured pruning skips channel aggregation and adds weight magnitude when curvature-derived scores vanish.
assumptions: A second-order expansion at the dense or current sparse checkpoint ranks the finite, often simultaneous deletion of parameters or channels well enough even when the pruning step leaves the local neighborhood.
The omitted higher-order Taylor terms and activation-region changes are small enough not to reorder candidate importance materially.
A finite sample of training batches estimates the deployment loss curvature and parameter ranking reliably.

The supported feed-forward computation graph can be decomposed into series paths and pairs of branches joined by matrix multiplication; recurrent state, arbitrary control flow, and unsupported operators are outside the derivation.
The operator-level Jacobian-vector rules used by the implementation match the actual forward graph and tensor layout.
Ignoring upper-layer bias cross terms is harmless for the weight-centered pruning experiments, despite the paper's broader parameter-level notation.
Summing weight scores into a channel or dependency group is an adequate proxy for deleting the group jointly.
Layerwise normalization makes scores comparable globally without erasing meaningful curvature scale differences.
FLOP count is an adequate deployment-cost proxy, even though structured shape, memory traffic, kernel selection, and hardware determine wall-clock latency.
Differences in dense checkpoints, data batches, fine-tuning, and baseline implementations do not explain the reported accuracy gaps.

techniques.role: Uses each coordinate's product with the Hessian-vector product as a second-order deletion-importance contribution.
Separates cross-layer curvature along differentiable upstream and downstream paths.
Accounts for cross-branch second derivatives induced when two parameterized branches meet in a matrix multiplication.
Propagates the sum of lower-layer directional perturbations without materializing full input Jacobians.
Specializes the parallel calculation to perturbations of query, key, value, softmax attention weights, and attention outputs.
Sums scores across input and output sides of structurally coupled layers before channel pruning.
Applies max, min-max, l2, or no normalization before comparing groups across layers.
Adds absolute weight magnitude in the unstructured route when vanishing gradients make the Taylor score uninformative.
Raises the pruning ratio over repeated steps until the measured model reaches a target retained-FLOP ratio.

limitations: Author-stated: the current derivation and implementation cover MLPs, CNNs, and Transformers, while RNNs, state-space models, and other time-series architectures require further work.
Reviewer-identified: exactness applies to the Hessian-vector term at one point, not to the finite loss change after pruning; higher-order Taylor terms are explicitly omitted.
Reviewer-identified: Equations 3 and 4 differ by a one-half factor on the quadratic contribution, which matters when first- and second-order terms are combined.

Reviewer-identified: Appendix E.1 incorrectly infers a zero mixed loss derivative from independence of lower-layer weights and upper-layer biases, leaving the all-parameter theorem unproved as stated.

Reviewer-identified: the derivation and released OBA implementation are operator-specific and contain an explicit not-implemented fallback, so support for a named architecture class does not imply support for arbitrary implementations of that class.
Reviewer-identified: no direct baseline compares JVPF against a standard automatic-differentiation Hessian-vector product for numerical equality, peak memory, or wall time.
Reviewer-identified: rank validation masks only a small, preselected set of ResNet32 neurons and reports no confidence intervals or variation across seeds, checkpoints, or batches.
Reviewer-identified: the structured results conflate importance quality with group construction, score normalization, pruning schedule, and up to 100-150 fine-tuning epochs.
Reviewer-identified: the all-layer rank table demonstrates normalization sensitivity; OBD or Taylor beats OBA in some cells despite the prose's broad superiority language.
Reviewer-identified: the claimed 0.79-point CIFAR-10 ResNet32 loss at roughly 6% retained FLOPs conflicts with the displayed 95.30% dense and 93.45% pruned accuracies.

Reviewer-identified: unstructured comparisons use different dense starting accuracies and substitute the cheaper CHITA-BSO variant for CHITA-CD on ResNet50; within-method ratios reduce but do not eliminate comparability concerns.
Reviewer-identified: FLOP-derived speed-up is not device latency, throughput, memory use, or energy, and unstructured sparsity may not accelerate ordinary dense kernels.

Reviewer-identified: the evaluation is confined to image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet with VGG, ResNet, and ViT; there are no language models, generative models, detection tasks, or distribution shifts.

Artifact audit: the current public repository at commit 91e27b2edcdfa4986dd14063e62f3684e453a754 provides an MIT-licensed pinned Conda environment and runnable entry scripts, but no tests, expected-result logs, pretrained CIFAR checkpoints, or versioned release artifacts.

Artifact audit: the repository's FastOBA implementation was added on 2025-06-17 after the v2 paper and can compute higher Taylor orders, but the paper contains no FastOBA experiments; it must not be treated as validation of the published results.

Artifact audit: ImageNet remains a manual external dependency, dataset paths require local editing, and experiment scripts enable Weights & Biases by default, so reproduction is not a single offline command.
failure_modes: A pruning step crosses ReLU or max-pooling boundaries, making curvature at the original active region a poor predictor of the new loss.
Many individually low-score parameters are removed together and their omitted higher-order or group interactions cause an abrupt accuracy collapse.
A mixed interaction involving a bias is important, but the derived upper-series calculation omits it.
A model uses an unsupported autograd operator, fused attention kernel, recurrent edge, custom control flow, or tensor layout and the hand-coded JVP path fails or computes the wrong surrogate.
Finite-batch curvature estimates are dominated by frequent classes and prune channels needed by rare examples or shifted inputs.
Layerwise max or min-max normalization is driven by an outlier, compressing the remaining scores and destabilizing global ranking.
Near-zero gradients cause the unstructured curvature score to vanish and the added magnitude term silently becomes the dominant criterion.
Pruned structured shapes reduce nominal FLOPs but map to inefficient kernels, so measured latency or energy does not improve.
Irregular unstructured sparsity retains accuracy but provides no speed-up on hardware without matching sparse kernels.
A baseline starts from a stronger dense checkpoint or receives a different fine-tuning budget, reversing the apparent method ranking under a controlled comparison.
Repeated score acquisition and graph retention exceed accelerator memory on larger Transformers even though the full Hessian is never materialized.
Attention implementations use masking, relative position biases, grouped-query attention, mixture-of-experts routing, or fused kernels not represented by the paper's QK-softmax-V path.
reusable_insights: Separate exact derivative computation from approximation of a finite intervention: an exact Hessian-vector product can still support only a local, truncated Taylor prediction.
Validate custom curvature propagation numerically against automatic differentiation on small networks before relying on its scaling advantage.
Treat biases, normalization parameters, and other parameter classes explicitly; parameter independence is not sufficient to remove mixed loss derivatives.
Measure both within-layer rank quality and cross-layer calibration because normalization can dominate a global pruning criterion.
Use operator-aware forward-mode propagation to reuse directional derivatives across many downstream layers when a generic full-graph transform is too memory intensive.
Model matrix multiplication as a distinct source of cross-branch curvature rather than treating a Transformer as only a serial stack.
Keep structural dependency grouping separate from importance estimation so either component can be ablated and reused.
Report dense checkpoint identity, score-acquisition batches, fine-tuning compute, and hardware latency alongside sparsity or FLOP ratios.
When a table and prose disagree, preserve the table values and flag the discrepancy instead of selecting the more favorable number.
Version code innovations added after publication separately from the artifact used to support the paper's empirical claims.
open_questions: Does the implemented OBA score numerically equal a reference automatic-differentiation Hessian-vector product for every supported parameter on small CNN and attention fixtures?
How should the missing one-half factor and mixed bias derivatives be corrected, and do the corrected scores change any pruning rankings?
Can generic forward-mode automatic differentiation replace the operator-specific JVP rules without losing the reported memory advantage?
How stable are rank correlations and final subnetworks across random seeds, curvature batches, dense checkpoints, and normalization choices?
Does OBA remain competitive when all methods share the same dense weights, exact pruning mask constraints, fine-tuning budget, and hardware target?
Do the FLOP reductions translate into latency, throughput, memory-energy, and carbon improvements on GPUs, CPUs, mobile accelerators, and sparse hardware?
Can the method support modern Transformer variants with fused attention, relative position bias, grouped-query attention, gated MLPs, mixture-of-experts routing, and very large language models?
Can group-level Hessian-vector scoring capture interactions among channels deleted simultaneously rather than summing coordinatewise values?
When does a Fisher or Gauss-Newton approximation rank pruning candidates as well as the true Hessian at far lower cost?
Can FastOBA's higher-order terms be evaluated under a fixed compute budget to determine whether they improve finite-pruning loss prediction?
What explains the 0.79-point CIFAR-10 claim that is inconsistent with Table 3, and which checkpoint-level values produced it?
Can the method be extended to recurrent and state-space architectures with a proof and implementation that handle parameter reuse over time?

competitive_landscape.title: Optimal Brain Damage
competitive_landscape.difference: Optimal Brain Damage uses a diagonal Hessian approximation to estimate the saliency of deleting one weight near a trained optimum. OBA retains cross-parameter Hessian-vector contributions along supported graph paths and applies them to structured as well as unstructured pruning, but inherits the local Taylor assumption.

competitive_landscape.title: EigenDamage: Structured Pruning in the Kronecker-Factored Eigenbasis
competitive_landscape.difference: EigenDamage approximates curvature with Kronecker factors, rotates parameters into a basis where weights are approximately independent, and prunes structured units there. OBA stays in the original parameterization and seeks direct coordinatewise Hessian-vector contributions through graph connectivity; EigenDamage remains a main experimental baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: Hessian-Aware Pruning and Optimal Neural Implant
competitive_landscape.difference: HAP ranks structured components with relative Hessian trace and replaces moderately sensitive components with low-rank neural implants, including CNN and Transformer-head experiments. OBA instead deletes dependency groups using per-coordinate Hessian-vector scores and does not introduce replacement modules.

competitive_landscape.title: DepGraph: Towards Any Structural Pruning
competitive_landscape.relationship: structural grouping foundation used by OBA
competitive_landscape.difference: DepGraph automatically discovers coupled parameter groups across CNNs, RNNs, GNNs, and Transformers and can prune them with simple norm scores. OBA reuses dependency grouping but contributes a curvature-based importance calculation; unlike DepGraph's broad grouping demonstration, OBA's derivative implementation supports a narrower operator family.

competitive_landscape.title: Fast as CHITA: Neural Network Pruning with Combinatorial Optimization
competitive_landscape.difference: CHITA jointly chooses and updates many weights under a sparsity constraint using a memory-friendly local quadratic model and combinatorial optimization. OBA primarily changes importance estimation and then ranks deletions, avoiding CHITA's optimization solve but not explicitly optimizing multi-weight cancellation; the paper compares against the cheaper CHITA-BSO variant on ResNet50.

competitive_landscape.title: FALCON: FLOP-Aware Combinatorial Optimization for Neural Network Pruning
competitive_landscape.difference: FALCON extends combinatorial pruning with explicit FLOP and sparsity constraints, using an integer-linear-program subproblem and approximate low-rank curvature structure. OBA gradually adjusts a rank threshold until a target FLOP ratio is crossed; it does not optimize the FLOP budget jointly with fidelity and sparsity. FALCON predates OBA's submission window but is absent from its related work and experiments.

competitive_landscape.title: Preserving Deep Representations In One-Shot Pruning: A Hessian-Free Second-Order Optimization Framework
competitive_landscape.difference: SNOWS uses automatic Hessian-vector products and conjugate gradients to readjust weights for a fixed mask under a multi-layer reconstruction objective, preserving deeper representations without materializing a Hessian. OBA uses graph-decomposed Hessian-vector contributions to choose the mask itself, then fine-tunes; the two methods address complementary selection and post-mask optimization stages, and SNOWS is not discussed in OBA.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first practical pruning method that directly computes each parameter's Hessian-vector product contribution, rather than approximating the Hessian with a diagonal or Fisher structure, by characterizing nonzero series and parallel layer interactions and evaluating them efficiently for CNNs and Transformers.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Theorems 4.2 and 4.4, JVPF, and Algorithm 1 present a concrete operator-aware decomposition; the comparison panel confirms that OBD, EigenDamage, HAP, and CHITA use diagonal, Kronecker/Fisher, trace, or quadratic-optimization alternatives. The ImageNet and CIFAR tables show that the resulting criterion can outperform the paper's selected baselines, while runtime measurements quantify its additional cost.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the combination of coordinatewise Hessian-vector importance, explicit series-versus-matrix-multiplication graph decomposition, attention-specific parallel terms, and dependency-group aggregation for mask selection. Exact Hessian-vector products themselves predate OBA, and concurrent SNOWS also uses exact Hessian products without forming the matrix. The broader claim of an exact second-order Taylor expansion for every parameter should be narrowed because the finite loss remains a truncated Taylor approximation, Equation 4 drops the one-half factor, the proof omits generally nonzero bias interactions, and the implementation is operator-specific. OBA is therefore a novel pruning-score construction and engineering path, not a general exact solution to finite network pruning.

reviewer_notes: Primary audit used the exact cached arXiv v2 PDF, whose hash and 19-page extraction lineage are recorded above. Every page was read and rendered: pages 1-13 contain the main paper and references, page 14 is a mostly blank final reference leaf, pages 15-19 contain implementation details, Algorithm 1, normalization formulas, Figure A1, and proofs. Visual inspection covered Figures 1-3 and A1, Tables 1-6, Algorithm 1, and displayed Equations 1-35; table values were taken from the rendered PDF when extracted text interleaved columns. The current official arXiv record still identifies v2 (2025-03-03), and the ICLR proceedings copy is consistent with the cached paper. Primary-literature queries covered the mechanism/task, evaluation/baselines, claimed novelty/predecessors, and later/concurrent second-order pruning work. The code artifact was inspected read-only at public main commit 91e27b2edcdfa4986dd14063e62f3684e453a754 (2025-06-17): it contains OBA/FastOBA pruners, experiment entry points, a pinned Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.0.1/CUDA 11.7 Conda environment, and Torch-Pruning-derived dependency code. No experiments were rerun because the repository does not ship the required ImageNet data or all dense checkpoints and the full workflows require many pruning/fine-tuning hours. The peer-review discussion could not be independently captured because OpenReview's forum and API presented a challenge page; no claim here depends on inaccessible reviewer text.
